chapter: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
title: "Lover Man" begins as a band theme
summary: He says "Lover Man" started as a scrap of paper used as the band's theme, and later got words much later after Europe.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Anyway, so it's good fortune. I mean, when you're young, you know, you don't think about it. "I'll write a million of them." I mean, it didn't matter. I didn't care.

Actually, as far as the song "Lover Man" came, it was a goof(?). The boys in the band used to laugh, because it was only a piece of paper. It was our theme song! [LAUGHS] And later on, it... I never thought it would make it as a
vocal. Somebody said, "Well, put words to it," so I put words to the song... At that time I had a friend of mine who... Anyway, I met Jimmy (?), a guy going into the Army, and this is how we made...
But this is much later now.
Very much later. That's after Europe. That's way after Europe.
It's not in context with what we're...
